correctness.rationale: For perfect structure matrices the squaring vectors are independent, forcing off-diagonal derivation coefficients to vanish. Diagonal Leibniz equations have one parameter precisely on each directed support component admitting cyclic r-coloring. An invertible color-compatible matrix has r equally sized color classes and r invertible off-diagonal blocks. Connected component exponential formulas then establish G_q(x)F_{q,r}(x^r)^{(u-1)/r}. Each good component has at least r vertices, yielding a sharp attainable dimension bound, and the first stratum consists of one weighted directed r-cycle plus any complement invertible block. An independently implemented full Leibniz-equation checker exhaustively verifies 13,963 matrices over small prime fields, with additional exact coefficient cases. Infinite validity rests on the complete proof rather than these finite tests.

value.rationale: The derivation Lie algebra records infinitesimal symmetries and its dimension is invariant under algebra isomorphism. A complete distribution over the canonical marked finite-field model is not obtained from the known structural graph criterion alone; the cyclic block determinant factor creates a nontrivial enumerative solution for all dimensions and fields. The exact characteristic-dependent first-occurrence threshold and all attainable dimensions distinguish algebraic resonance from generic rigidity. The result is not an arbitrary narrow numerical sample.
